direct_answer: Smart speakers can help with reminders, calls, music and controlling lights or heating without using stiff hands. They are not a replacement for a community alarm or 999 in an emergency. Ask someone you trust to help set one up.

content:
Voice control can help when hands are stiff or moving is tiring.

This guide covers uses and limits. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Useful uses

  • Medicine reminders.
  • Calling family.
  • Smart plugs for lamps.
  • Radio and audiobooks.

Limits

Do not rely on a smart speaker for emergencies. Check whether it can call emergency services where you live; a community alarm may be safer.

Privacy

  • Check privacy settings.
  • Mute the microphone when wanted.

Getting set up

Ask family, a local library or a charity for help.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Do I need Wi-Fi?

Usually yes.

Can it call 999?

Do not rely on it.

Sources and further reading

Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
